Objects of packaging.pylock and packaging.direct_url that were pickled by packaging 26.3 (and 26.0, 26.1) load as garbage with this version: no error, but every field holds its own name.

```python
# written with packaging 26.3:
import pickle
from packaging.direct_url import DirectUrl, VcsInfo
data = pickle.dumps(DirectUrl(url="https://g.c/r.git", vcs_info=VcsInfo(vcs="git", commit_id="a" * 40)))

# loaded with this version:
pickle.loads(data)
# DirectUrl(url='url', archive_info='archive_info', vcs_info='vcs_info', dir_info='dir_info', subdirectory='subdirectory')
```

The same happens to Pylock and every dataclass it contains (packages, wheels, sdists, vcs/directory/archive entries...). The older releases stored the instance __dict__ as the pickle state.

Expected:
- pickles written by packaging 26.0, 26.1 and 26.3 of any dataclass in packaging.pylock and packaging.direct_url (nested ones included) load into objects equal to the originals, with nested objects of the right types;
- pickling and copy.deepcopy with this version keep working as they do now;
- an old-style dict state whose keys are not exactly the dataclass's fields (a field missing, or an unknown key) raises TypeError, and the message names the class (e.g. "DirectUrl").

The test venv's site-packages has packaging 26.3 installed, if you want to produce old pickles.
